key_insight: A multi-fidelity CAE transfer-learning pipeline can learn damage localization and sizing from large synthetic guided-wave data and adapt effectively to sparse experimental measurements.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to deploy accurate structural health monitoring on plate-like structures without requiring large labeled experimental datasets.
method: Train a lightweight 1D time-domain spectral element model to generate large simulated guided-wave data.
Pretrain a convolutional autoencoder to learn compact damage features, then transfer to a feed-forward predictor.
Fine-tune the model with a small labeled experimental set for domain adaptation and damage inference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong performance with R² > 0.93 for damage localization and R² > 0.99 for damage sizing, including good generalization to unseen damage cases.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on how well the synthetic simulation matches the real experimental wave propagation and sensor conditions.
paper_title: A Multi-Fidelity Convolutional Autoencoder-Transfer Learning Framework for Guided-Wave-Based Damage Diagnosis Using Large Simulated and Limited Experimental Datasets
